text:
incident-bot: PAGER: P1 network/service-discovery in us-west-2c - spike in SRV lookup timeouts and 5xx errors for internal platform services. Paging oncall.
Maya (sre): I'm seeing a big uptick in internal 5xx for customer-facing inference in us-west-2. Root cause looks like SRV lookups failing to return endpoints intermittently.
Aisha (oncall): I'm on it. Do we have any alert graphs? Link: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/1728345600
Maya (sre): Yes - lookup latency from app-proxy -> coredns spikes from ~5ms to ~800ms and a lot of UDP retransmits. svc-discovery errors up 12x. Customer-facing 503 increase.
Ravi (infra): Quick check: coreDNS pods in us-west-2c are up. kube-proxy logs show some 403s on iptables sync but not huge. Could be network-level drop to kube-dns service VIP.
Kevin (net): We're seeing a packet loss pattern on the AZ peering fabric for us-west-2c for UDP flows. BGP counters show route flaps toward the AZ edge. Suspect blackhole to the nodes hosting coredns.
Joel (svc-discovery): Consul health in that AZ looks ok but SRV lookups from nodes in us-west-2c to Consul sometimes time out before fallback. Consul agent logs show occasional connection resets.
Maya (sre): Customer impact: ~30% of requests hitting backend in 2c getting 502/503. Other AZs healthy. Workload autoscaler is retrying but amplifying lookups.
Emily (cs): We have 3 paying customers reporting increased 5xx in that region. Escalating to account teams. ETA for mitigation?
Aisha (oncall): Short-term mitigation options: 1) Evacuate critical replicas from us-west-2c to 2a/2b 2) Force app-proxy to prefer endpoints in healthy AZ 3) Bump coredns replicas in other AZs and change service endpoints.
Tanya (eng): We can do route-preference by updating internal service shard affinity quickly. I'll prepare a canary patch to set prefer-az header at proxy for retries.
ops-bot: runbook-snippet: to temporarily avoid AZ DNS failures you can:
```
kubectl patch svc kube-dns -n kube-system --type=json -p='[ {"op":"replace","path":"/spec/externalTrafficPolicy","value":"Local"} ]'
```
(only if you understand kube NAT implications)
Kevin (net): I will open a ticket with cloud provider and confirm peering counters. Meanwhile, Ravi can we taint nodes in 2c to force pods to reschedule out?
Ravi (infra): We can cordon a subset of nodes in 2c for non-critical workloads. Forcing eviction for critical customer pods needs careful order. I'll start with scaling down non-prod and move one backend at a time.
Maya (sre): Action plan now: (A) Put app-proxy on prefer-healthy-az routing (Tanya) (B) Cordon non-critical nodes in 2c (Ravi) (C) Bump timeouts and circuit-breakers to reduce retries (Joel) (D) Net team engages cloud (Kevin).
Joel (svc-discovery): Also changing Consul SRV TTL temporarily to 10s to speed up failover. Doing now via API for the service namespace `inference-backend`.
Tanya (eng): Pushing small proxy config: prefer_az=2a, fallback=2b for active routes. Rolling to 5% first.
Maya (sre): Rolling updates started. Observability: SRV lookup errors down a bit but still elevated.
incident-bot: deploy-bot: rollout started by Tanya (eng) 1728345712 -> 5% canary
Kevin (net): Cloud says their internal peering saw a micro-outage affecting UDP cloning to 2c for ~3 minutes, then intermittent drops. They are routing around but still seeing higher drop rates.
Ravi (infra): Cordon started. Evicting non-prod. Will not evict critical stateful until we confirm leader handoffs for Consul/etcd.
Joel (svc-discovery): Confirmed: consul leader remains in 2b, consul agents in 2c are flapping their connection to seed nodes due to TCP resets. For SRV path, some queries fall back to UDP retransmit which then hits the blackhole.
Maya (sre): Immediate mitigation effective: app-proxy prefer-az reduced customer 5xx by ~70% for traffic that routed to other AZs. But any pods resident in 2c still affected.
Emily (cs): Notifying affected customers with an intermediate update. Template: "We have localized DNS/service discovery issue in us-west-2c; mitigation in flight; some API requests may see transient errors."
Aisha (oncall): Handoff: I'm handing oncall to Kevin (network) for next 90 minutes while I assist with prods scaling. Kevin please accept.
Kevin (net): Accepted. I'll own until 1728345965. Focus: keep cloud engaged and validate peering fix.
ops-bot: pager-note: oncall handoff recorded: from Aisha to Kevin
Tanya (eng): Canary at 5% looks good. Rolling to 50%.
Maya (sre): Observed spike in SRV resolution failures reduce as canary grows. We'll keep rolling if metrics stay normal for 3m.
Kevin (net): Cloud confirms a faulty forwarder instance in the peering fabric has been replaced; counters improved but need sustained 10m of stability. Monitoring BGP state.
Joel (svc-discovery): I'm going to pump up consul TTLs back to sane levels once fabric stable. For now left at 10s. Also disabling aggressive retry path in client library to avoid cascading DNS storms.
Maya (sre): Customer impact assessment: ~45k requests affected in 30m window, error budget burn for us-west-2 ~0.8%. Major customers have been notified. No data loss reported.
Ravi (infra): Uncordon strategy: we'll keep critical pods drained out of 2c until Cloud gives explicit stable round of 10m. Nodes will remain schedulable only for infra-critical daemons.
Aisha (oncall): Confirming we did not change production DNS records or public-facing routes. This is internal service discovery only.
Tanya (eng): Rollout to 100% complete. Metrics look within normal bounds for canary traffic.
incident-bot: deploy-bot: rollout complete 1728345850 by Tanya (eng)
Kevin (net): Continuing to watch for 5m. If drops return, next step is to fail traffic entirely away from 2c via route policy (requires infra coord).
Maya (sre): Ok hold for 10m stabilizing window. If stable, we'll close incident and open postmortem doc.
Emily (cs): Sending customer follow-up: "Mitigation applied; we expect near-full recovery in the next few minutes; we'll send full postmortem." :thumbsup:
Joel (svc-discovery): Creating postmortem stub: https://docs.redwood/incidents/1728345600-srv-azc-blackhole/ - will fill with timeline, root cause, mitigations, and follow-ups (reduce SRV retries, prefer-az controls, cloud escalation plan).
Aisha (oncall): Thanks all. If you see anything odd ping @oncall-sre. I'll stay nearby for final verification.
Kevin (net): 3m stable and packet counters trending down. Cloud keeping the flow steering in place.
Maya (sre): 10m window passed. SRV lookup latency back to baseline, 5xx rates normal. Moving to resolved state but postmortem required.
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED: P1 network/service-discovery us-west-2c at 1728345965 - mitigation applied, monitoring healthy.
Maya (sre): Postmortem owners: Joel (svc-discovery), Kevin (net), Ravi (infra). Immediate follow-ups: add route-failure playbook, automatic AZ-preference for app-proxy, validate consul health-checks on peering flaps.
Emily (cs): I'll coordinate customer comms and attach timeline once postmortem is ready.
ops-bot: note: retention tag set: incident/needs-postmortem
Maya (sre): Thanks everyone. Closing thread for now. If any regressions reopen channel.
